title: FARDC-Wazalendo Retake Miko Hill in Masisi as Army Launches Offensive on Mindjendje
detail: Government forces backed by Wazalendo fighters recaptured the strategic Miko hill in Katuunda locality, Ufamandu 1er grouping (Masisi territory), on Tuesday, Sept 15, after particularly heavy fighting with AFC/M23 rebels; the position allows monitoring of several routes toward Walikale and is considered militarily significant. The same day, roughly 30km northwest in Walikale's Kisimba grouping, FARDC and Wazalendo launched an offensive to retake the Mindjendje position (Banakindi locality) that AFC/M23 had held since Sept 10; after several hours of combat, rebels withdrew toward Malemo in neighboring Masisi. Separately, traffic timidly resumed on the Kashebere-Mungazi axis in Walikale's Luberike grouping after FARDC and Wazalendo forces briefly occupied and then withdrew from Kibati.

confidenceReason: Reported by two independent Congolese outlets citing local and administrative sources; no FARDC or M23 official statement and no casualty figures were available for either front.

title: C64 Opposition March Draws Bans, Arrests and Fayulu's 'Ambush' Accusation Against Tshisekedi
detail: The Coalition Article 64's nationwide march against President Tshisekedi's constitutional referendum push went ahead Tuesday, Sept 15, under heavy security. In Kinshasa, an eleventh-hour route agreement between C64 and city hall let activists converge on the Limete interchange and march through Bandal toward the Moulaert roundabout, but opposition leader Martin Fayulu accused the regime of setting an 'ambush,' saying members of the pro-government Force du Progrès armed with bladed weapons had been placed among police ostensibly securing the march. Authorities banned or blocked the march in several provinces: police used tear gas to disperse demonstrators in Kananga and arrested several activists and party officials; in Lubumbashi, police dispersed a gathering at Forrest Square and detained roughly 20 activists, including deputy Christian Mwando's entourage, while deputy Khiller Mubambe was briefly held then released; authorities in Gemena, Mbuji-Mayi and Kisangani barred any assembly, citing security concerns and, in Kisangani's case, the Ebola outbreak. The march proceeded largely unimpeded in Bandundu (Kwilu) despite one party office being barricaded. Security sources said no deaths were recorded amid roughly 20-plus arrests nationwide. Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya on Sept 16 accused the opposition of manipulation over the march's conduct.

media.caption: Opposition activists march toward Kinshasa's Moulaert roundabout during the C64 coalition's nationwide protest, Sept 15, 2026

confidenceReason: March locations, bans and arrest counts are corroborated by Radio Okapi (tier 2) and CongoQuotidien; Fayulu's 'ambush' allegation is his own account and has not been independently confirmed or addressed by government forces.
